title: HCP introduces IBMid support and new enterprise governance capabilities
content:
Over the past quarter, the HashiCorp Cloud Platform (HCP) team has continued investing in the foundations that help organizations securely adopt and operate HashiCorp products at scale.

These updates focus on four pillars of the HCP experience: identity, governance, access management, and lifecycle administration, making it easier to manage access, enforce organizational standards, and streamline day-to-day operations. The recent platform enhancements include:

  • IBMid to Sign in to HCP Services

  • Enterprise constraints for centralized governance

  • Streamlined user onboarding and access assignment

  • Self-service HCP account removal

  • Self-service organization deletion

IBMid to Sign in to HCP Services

What's new: We are introducing the general availability of IBMid as a sign-in method for HCP accounts. IBMid sign-in gives users additional authentication options, including Google, GitHub, and email-based authentication. It also provides a single identity across IBM products, expanded multi-factor authentication (MFA) options, and easier access to IBM support.

If you already have an IBMid whose email address matches the one on your HCP account, you can use it to sign in today. If you don't have one, create an IBMid with the same email address as your HCP account. This links your existing access, so you can sign in without disruption.

Benefits:

  • One identity across IBM products and support: Use the same IBMid for HCP, other IBM products, and support, with no separate HCP credentials to manage.

  • Flexible sign-in options with stronger authentication: Choose Google, GitHub, or email-and-password when creating your IBMid. Additionally, IBMid provides additional multi-factor authentication (MFA) options.

To learn more, check out the create an HCP account documentation.

Enterprise constraints for centralized governance

Feature gap: As organizations adopt more cloud services, platform teams often need governance controls that extend beyond user permissions alone. Even when role-based access controls are in place, enterprises may need additional guardrails to manage consumption costs, enforce security reviews, and ensure only approved products are deployed across the organization.

What's new: We are introducing Enterprise constraints for HCP. Available to all HCP organizations, Enterprise constraints allow administrators to restrict which HCP products can be deployed within their organization. Unlike RBAC, which determines who can perform actions, Enterprise constraints determine what products can be created, providing an additional layer of governance that applies consistently across all projects.

Benefits:

  • Stronger governance controls: Ensure only approved HCP products can be deployed across your organization.

  • Improved cost management: Help control consumption spending by limiting access to products that are not intended for organizational use.

  • Consistent policy enforcement: Apply organization-wide guardrails that cannot be bypassed through project-level permissions or role assignments.

  • Simplified compliance management: Support internal security and regulatory requirements by ensuring approved product standards are enforced centrally.

To learn more and get started, see the enterprise constraints documentation.

Streamlined user onboarding and access assignment

Feature gap: As organizations grow, administrators need to quickly grant users access to the right resources. Previously, inviting a user and assigning their permissions could require multiple administrative steps, creating additional overhead when onboarding team members and collaborators.

What's new: We have streamlined user onboarding in HCP. Administrators can now assign roles to users as part of the invitation workflow, either through the organization IAM policy or directly within a project IAM policy. Available to all HCP organizations, this enhancement reduces the number of steps required to provision access and helps ensure users receive the appropriate permissions from day one.

Benefits:

  • Faster user onboarding: Grant access and permissions through a single workflow instead of multiple administrative actions.

  • Reduced administrative effort: Eliminate manual follow-up steps when provisioning new users.

  • Improved access consistency: Help ensure users receive the appropriate permissions at the time they are invited.

  • Accelerated team productivity: Enable new team members and collaborators to get started more quickly.

To learn more, check out the invite users documentation.

Self-service HCP account removal

Feature gap: While many organizations use SSO and SCIM to automate user lifecycle management, HCP users may still maintain local accounts authenticated with email and password or GitHub. Historically, permanently removing these accounts required engaging support teams, creating additional friction for users who wanted to close their account or remove personal data from HCP.

What's new: We are introducing self-service account removal for HCP. Available to users who authenticate with email and password or GitHub, this capability allows users to permanently remove their HCP account directly from the HCP portal without opening a support case.

Benefits:

  • Greater user control: Allow users to manage their own account lifecycle without requiring support engagement.

  • Improved privacy management: Simplify account removal for users who no longer wish to maintain an HCP account.

  • Reduced support overhead: Eliminate manual support requests for account deletion and cleanup.

  • Better self-service experience: Give users a straightforward way to remove unused or no-longer-needed accounts.

To learn more, check out the HCP account documentation.

Self-service organization deletion

Feature gap: As organizations evaluate cloud services, consolidate environments, or retire projects, administrators need an efficient way to decommission unused organizations. Historically, deleting an HCP organization required engaging support, creating additional operational steps and slowing environment cleanup.

What's new: We are introducing self-service organization deletion for HCP. Available to all HCP organizations, Organization owners can now delete organizations directly from the HCP portal. Built-in safety checks help ensure required prerequisites are met before deletion occurs.

Benefits:

  • Greater administrative control: Manage the complete organization lifecycle directly within HCP.

  • Faster environment cleanup: Retire unused organizations without waiting on support engagement.

  • Reduced operational friction: Eliminate manual processes when consolidating or decommissioning environments.

  • Improved governance and lifecycle management: Help maintain a cleaner, more intentional HCP footprint over time.

To learn more, check out the organization documentation.

Explore the latest HCP enhancements

These updates are part of our ongoing investment in making HCP the easiest way to securely discover, access, and operate HashiCorp products in the cloud. Whether you're deploying infrastructure with Terraform, managing secrets with Vault, or adopting additional HCP services, these capabilities help platform teams strengthen governance, simplify administration, and reduce operational overhead.

To learn more, sign in to your HCP organization, explore the linked documentation, or create an HCP account to get started.
author: Trevor Powell
